utility.notes: Mill Valley is a well-documented Marin County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy)
value.notes: MCE's own service-area page confirms Mill Valley as one of Marin County's member communities. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_authority.value: City of Mill Valley Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Mill Valley/Marin County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

required_documents.notes: The Building Official has adopted a checklist for small residential rooftop solar energy systems, and a separate Structural Criteria document exists for expedited permitting, but the specific document list was not directly enumerated in the page content reviewed this session.

value: Schedule inspections online (permits must have status 'issued'); have ETrakIT username/password, permit number, property address, and inspection type ready
Cutoff for scheduling is 3pm the day before the requested inspection date; requests can be made up to 7 days in advance
Approximate inspection time windows are 8-10am, 10am-noon, 1-3pm, and 3-5pm; no inspections on Fridays
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: The City's own page is titled 'How to Apply for Instant Permits in Mill Valley' and describes 'Benefits of Instant Solar Permits' via its Symbium-based automated permitting platform (SB 379 compliance).

other_conditions: The checklist and permitting documentation conform to recommendations for expedited permitting in the California Solar Permitting Guidebook
The city provides a separate Structural Criteria document addressing roof loading and support requirements for expedited permitting
